reason: I'll follow the moon-bearing rocky world first, matching the goal about its remaining stones.
expectation: I expect to place the world in the disk and perhaps see it encounter rocky material; the exact result is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: The exposed gas may address the other goal, but I prefer to follow the rocky world first.

effect: The rocky world encountered the remaining stones, completing its goal; I can now follow material elsewhere in the system.
reaction: The widened view makes the world's continuity with its moon clear.
reason: I'll follow the exposed gas and dust to see whether it returns material to the surrounding galaxy.
expectation: I expect the exposed inner disk to disperse some gas and dust, though its destination is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: The inward-moving icy body may also reveal a fate of material, but I'll follow the gas first.

effect: The gas and dust escaped into the surrounding nursery, clarifying how disk material returns to the galaxy.
reaction: The contrast between retained worlds and dispersed birth material is satisfying.
reason: I'll follow the inward-moving icy body; it's the only offered gameplay action and may address the remaining goal.
expectation: I expect the icy body to change as it enters the exposed inner disk, though its fate is uncertain.

effect: The icy body sheds gas and dust in the warm inner disk while its nucleus survives.
reaction: The distinction between a bright tail and the surviving nucleus is clear.
reason: I'll combine the shedding body with the projectiles; it's the only offered gameplay action and may advance the remaining goal.
expectation: I expect a collision to alter or break the icy body, though the outcome is uncertain.

effect: The projectile broke the active nucleus into fragments and exposed fresh ice; I'll follow those pieces in the inner disk.
reaction: The collision gives the earlier shedding body a distinct fate.
reason: This is the only offered gameplay action, and it follows the newly exposed fragments.
expectation: I expect the fragments to warm and shed more gas and dust, though their ultimate fate is uncertain.

effect: The exposed ice escaped, leaving rocky grains and rubble to follow among the planets.
reaction: The fragments' progression from icy body to rocky remains is clear.
reason: I'll combine the remains with the shattered body's fragments; it's the only offered gameplay action and follows the remaining material.
expectation: I expect the two sets of rocky fragments to become part of the debris among the planets, though the exact result is uncertain.

effect: The icy body's rocky remains mixed with the shattered-body fragments, completing the remaining goal.
reaction: The two material histories meeting between the planets was a satisfying conclusion.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following disk gas and dust back into the nursery connected the planetary system to the wider galactic story.

leastWorthwhile.text: The sequence following the icy body was clear, but became repetitive because each step offered only one gameplay action.

surprise.text: The icy body's tail did not mean the nucleus had disappeared; a later collision exposed fresh ice.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, although the final mixing was a prescribed action rather than a compatibility I discovered.

continue.text: I would continue for another chapter to see how the connected material histories develop, though I would hope for more meaningful choices.
